entry.title: How Sustainable Are AI Data Centers? Energy, Water, Raw Materials & Life Cycle Assessment Explained

media:group.media:title: How Sustainable Are AI Data Centers? Energy, Water, Raw Materials & Life Cycle Assessment Explained
media:group.media:description:
*How sustainable are AI data centers? What impact do artificial intelligence, increasing computing power, and modern IT infrastructures have on energy consumption, water usage, and resource consumption?*
In this online expert session, Dr. Lutz Stobbe from Fraunhofer IZM provides in-depth insight into current developments surrounding data centers and AI data centers. The presentation highlights technical, economic, and environmental trends and demonstrates how the environmental impacts of digital infrastructures can be assessed using life cycle assessments and life cycle assessments.
Data centers form the backbone of the digital society. With the rapid growth of AI-based applications, the global demand for high-performance IT infrastructure is rising. At the same time, issues related to energy efficiency, resource conservation, and sustainable digitalization are becoming increasingly important.
*Key Topics:*
• The AI Boom: Developments, Market Trends, and Forecasts • Energy consumption of data centers and AI data centers • Water and raw material requirements of digital infrastructures • Life cycle assessment (LCA) methods • Life cycle assessment of a high-performance server • Environmental impacts of hardware manufacturing and operation • Eco-efficiency of data centers and IT systems • Prospects for a more sustainable digital infrastructure
*Chapter:* 00:00 Welcome & Introduction 01:19 Market Outlook: Global Trends & Impacts 14:11 Relevant technological developments, including processor energy efficiency, cooling requirements, and the impact of the carbon footprint on semiconductor manufacturing 30:21 Energy consumption of data centers in Germany 31:50 Guidelines for data collection to support environmental assessment and eco-design 33:40 Conclusion
🎥 Green ICT Developments – The Fraunhofer IZM Expert Series
This video is Part 1 of 3 in our expert series on sustainable information and communication technology.
Over the next few weeks, two more expert presentations will follow, in which researchers from Fraunhofer IZM will discuss current developments, methods, and challenges related to Green ICT, environmental assessment, and sustainable digitalization.
✅ Part 1: Environmental and Technology Trends in Data Centers and AI Data Centers (this video) ⏳ Part 2: Coming soon ⏳ Part 3: Coming soon
Subscribe to our channel and turn on notifications so you don’t miss the next episodes.
*More information on the expert series:* https://www.izm.fraunhofer.de/de/events/green-ict-developments/

media:group.media:title: High-Frequency Microelectronics Laboratory | Testing and Validation of RF & Sensor Systems
media:group.media:description:
Today, new electronics must deliver higher performance, greater energy efficiency, and increased reliability than ever before. At the same time, expectations regarding development time, product quality, and resource efficiency continue to grow.
The Laboratory for High-Frequency Microelectronics at Fraunhofer IZM supports companies throughout the development and qualification of advanced electronic systems. We analyze materials, characterize RF and high-frequency components, validate emerging technologies, and optimize the energy consumption of electronic systems from the earliest development stages.
From initial concepts and prototyping to technology qualification, our partners benefit from state-of-the-art laboratory infrastructure, scientific excellence, and extensive experience from research and industrial projects.

entry.title: 3D X-Ray Microscopy for Advanced Packaging and Chiplet Integration

media:group.media:title: 3D X-Ray Microscopy for Advanced Packaging and Chiplet Integration
media:group.media:description:
#BuildingAPECS I 4/4
As part of the ongoing expansion of the APECS Pilot Line, a new 3D X-ray microscope was installed at Fraunhofer IZM. Since the system was too heavy for the freight elevator, it had to be lifted by crane through a second-floor laboratory window.
The microscope enables high-resolution 3D imaging at the submicrometer scale. It expands capabilities for nondestructive analysis of packaging structures, interconnection technologies, and integrated microelectronic systems.
The system supports research in advanced packaging, chiplet integration, and system integration and strengthens the APECS Pilot Line as research infrastructure for advanced packaging and microelectronics.
Part 4 of 4 of the #BuildingAPECS series documenting the development of the APECS Pilot Line at Fraunhofer IZM.
As the APECS Pilot Line continues to take shape, it is creating research infrastructure for the next generation of microelectronics technologies. Our sincere thanks go to everyone involved in planning, procurement, logistics, cleanroom operations, and research whose dedication makes this effort possible.
About APECS
APECS (Advanced Packaging and Integration for Electronic Components and Systems) is a pilot line established under the EU Chips Act as part of the Chips for Europe Initiative. The pilot line strengthens Europe's capabilities in advanced packaging and heterogeneous system integration and supports the transition from research to industrial application.
APECS is coordinated by Fraunhofer and implemented together with the Research Fab Microelectronics Germany (FMD) and leading research organizations across Europe.
The project is funded through the Chips Joint Undertaking (supported by Horizon Europe and the Digital Europe Programme) and co-funded by national funding programs in several European countries.

entry.title: New Capabilities for 2D and 3D Wafer and Panel Inspection

media:group.media:title: New Capabilities for 2D and 3D Wafer and Panel Inspection
media:group.media:description:
#BuildingAPECS I 2/4
As part of the expansion of the APECS Pilot Line, a new inspection microscope was integrated at Fraunhofer IZM. The system enables flexible 2D and 3D inspection of wafers, panels, advanced packaging structures, and microelectronic components.
This time-lapse video documents a multi-day process: cleanroom preparation and modifications, equipment delivery, and final integration. Existing systems were protected from potential contamination throughout the work.
The inspection microscope expands analytical capabilities across the microelectronics process chain and supports research in advanced packaging, chiplet integration, and system integration. It strengthens the APECS Pilot Line as research infrastructure for advanced packaging and microelectronics.

entry.title: Recycled Plastics in Electronics: A Systems Perspective

media:group.media:title: Recycled Plastics in Electronics: A Systems Perspective
media:group.media:description:
#CircularEconomy #CircularDesign #Recycling
How can recycled plastics become a viable resource for the European electronics industry?
This animated explainer presents the INCREACE project’s systems perspective on recycled plastics in the European electronics value chain.
Using a causal loop diagram and the iceberg model, the video illustrates why technological innovation alone is not enough. Supply and demand, consumer behaviour, public policy, product design, and underlying system structures all influence the transition towards a circular plastics economy.
The European INCREACE project works to improve the availability and quality of recycled plastics through innovative recycling processes, promote their use in high-value products, and strengthen collaboration across the value chain.
Learn more about the INCREACE project: https://increace-project.eu/

entry.title: From Truck to Cleanroom: Building the APECS Pilot Line

media:group.media:title: From Truck to Cleanroom: Building the APECS Pilot Line
media:group.media:description:
#BuildingAPECS I 1/4
Research begins long before the first experiment. In early 2026, numerous shipping crates containing a new ashing and etching chamber arrived at Fraunhofer IZM when temperatures were around 14°F (−10°C). The system will become part of the APECS Pilot Line, research infrastructure for advanced packaging and microelectronics.
Before the components could be integrated into the cleanroom, they had to be unloaded, sorted, unpacked, and prepared for installation. The ashing and etching chamber expands capabilities for wafer processing and supports research in advanced packaging, chiplet integration, and system integration.
This video highlights an often unseen aspect of modern research infrastructure: delivering and preparing complex equipment that enables future research and development.
Part 1 of 4 of the #BuildingAPECS series documenting the development of the APECS Pilot Line at Fraunhofer IZM.
About APECS
APECS (Advanced Packaging and Integration for Electronic Components and Systems) is a pilot line established under the EU Chips Act as part of the Chips for Europe Initiative. The pilot line strengthens Europe's capabilities in advanced packaging and heterogeneous system integration and supports the transition from research to industrial application.
APECS is coordinated by Fraunhofer and implemented together with the Research Fab Microelectronics Germany (FMD) and leading research organizations across Europe.
The project is funded through the Chips Joint Undertaking (supported by Horizon Europe and the Digital Europe Programme) and co-funded by national funding programs in several European countries.
